docs.summary: A live world of GameObjects. Its stored form is a [`SceneAsset`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.SceneAsset), and any number of scenes can be instantiated from one, like the editor's edit copy and play copy.

The currently active scene. There is always one: reading this before anything has been loaded creates an empty scene, so the engine is never in a no-scene state and callers never have to handle null. Use [`Load`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Scene~Load) to replace it.
Fires after a scene is loaded via Load().
Whether a [`Load`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Scene~Load) is queued and has not been applied yet, so [`Current`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Scene~Current) is still the outgoing scene.

Queues a scene to become the current one, replacing the previously loaded scene. The swap happens at the end of the frame, alongside the destroy queue, so the outgoing scene stays usable for everything still running this frame.
Loads a stored scene and everything it uses, blocking, and makes it current at the end of the frame.

Loads a stored scene and everything it uses in the background while the current scene keeps running, and makes it current at the end of the frame the loading finishes on. A second load cancels this one.
Builds a live scene from a stored one, without making it current.
The stored scene this one was instantiated from, if any. Not held, since a live scene no longer needs its stored form.

Keeps a GameObject alive across scene loads. It moves straight from the outgoing scene to the incoming one when the swap applies, so it is never held by a scene that is about to be disposed, and it is not disabled and re-enabled on the way.

Only roots can be preserved, since half a hierarchy surviving a load is never what was meant. Passing a child preserves its root instead.
Stops preserving a GameObject. It stays in whatever scene it is in now, and goes with that scene on the next load.
Whether this GameObject (or the root it belongs to) survives scene loads.

Applies a queued [`Load`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Scene~Load). Driven once per frame by the game loop, right after the destroy queue. Nothing is mid-callback at that point, so the outgoing scene is disposed outright rather than queued for another frame.
This scene's navigation state (registered navmeshes, queries, crowd).
Every animator in the scene, advanced once per frame in its own phase.
The scene's link to Graphite: its render world and what keeps state in it.
The scene's sky, ambient light and fog.
Runtime probe sampler built from [`BakedLighting`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Scene~BakedLighting) (lazy). Null when there are no baked probes.
Drop the cached probe volume so the next access rebuilds it (call after a rebake).
The number of registered, non-disposed objects.
Enumerates all registered objects.
Enumerates all registered objects that are currently active and saveable.
Enumerates all registered objects that are currently active.
Enumerates all root GameObjects, i.e. all GameObjects without a parent object.
Enumerates all [`RootObjects`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Scene~RootObjects) that are currently active.
Returns whether this Scene is completely empty.
Returns whether this scene is currently active.
Creates a new, empty scene which does not contain any [`GameObjects`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameObject).
Enables this scene, triggering OnEnable callbacks for its components. For most use cases, prefer using Scene.Load() instead of calling Enable() directly.
Disables this scene, triggering OnDisable callbacks for its components. For most use cases, prefer using Scene.Unload() or Scene.Load() instead of calling Disable() directly.
Registers a GameObject and all of its children.

docs.remarks: Asking to remove something this scene does not hold is reported rather than ignored. It leaves the object ticking in whichever scene does hold it, which reads as the engine having ignored the call.

Runs Start, then Update, then LateUpdate for the scene's registered components (those that implement those callbacks and are enabled in an active scene), in execution order. Each call is still gated per-component by ShouldExecuteGameplay.
Executes physics update on all active GameObjects and their components. FixedUpdate is gated internally by each component's ShouldExecuteGameplay.
Collects render data from all active components for the given camera. Components add their renderables and lights to the provided lists.
Executes GUI update on all active GameObjects and their components. Calls OnGUI.
